1.note: Ps 68:14 "if you lie among the שְׁפַתַּיִם", a word of unsure sense (sheepfolds, or the stones on which a pot is set). Next to "oven and stove" it is read here as the hearthstones: she is always in the kitchen.

2.he: וּכְלֵי קְרָב הַבֶּטֶן שׁוֹת שָׁתוּ הַשַּעַר
2.note: Isa 22:7 "the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate". קְרָב is "battle", but it also sounds like קֶרֶב "inward parts": the belly's hunger is a siege. The pun cannot be carried over.

3.note: "A need" (צֹרֶךְ) is also the usual polite word for relieving oneself, which is why the host at once shows his guest the privy.

4.note: Ps 109:14 has the divine name; here it is written as אדוני, the word the merchant uses for "my lord" all through the gate, so the curse can also be heard as addressed to the listener.

5.note: "I compose compositions" (אחבר מחברות) plays on the speaker's name, Ḥever (חֶבֶר), in the line before.
